title: Least-Squares Fit
summary: Fit a line by hand to sleep and morale, see what least squares minimises, then let lm() do it.
hints: `fit <- lm(morale_score ~ sleep_hours, data = d)`: outcome on the left of `~`, predictor on the right. `coef(fit)` gives intercept and slope.
`sum(residuals(fit)^2)` is the SSE; `sum((d$morale_score - mean(d$morale_score))^2)` is the SST.

goals.text: Move the line until your SSE is within **25%** of the least-squares minimum, without showing the least-squares line.
goals.detail: Watch the squares: a line close to most points but far from a few still pays for those few, squared.

goals.text: Get within **2%** of the minimum, still without peeking.
goals.detail: There is exactly one line with the smallest SSE. That's the least-squares line, and it's what `lm()` finds.

goals.text: Set the **slope to 0** and find the best **flat** line.
goals.detail: The best flat line sits at the mean of y. Its SSE is the total sum of squares (SST), and R² = 1 − SSE/SST compares any line with it.
